verbs.name: screen_record.rehearsal_start
verbs.description: Capture one disposable 3- to 5-second native screen rehearsal from the currently selected display or opaque window identity, then return only a revocable opaque playback handle and same-origin playback URL. It does not require, create, open, save, or mutate a project; it creates no recovery marker, checkpoint, capture journal, RecordingProject, Studio event, or timeline media. The bounded temporary bytes are owned solely by cutd, cannot be promoted implicitly, and are discarded when the UI closes playback, starts another rehearsal, or starts an ordinary recording. The normal recorder capability/target admission still applies. This video-only test deliberately does not open microphone or system-audio streams; use the explicit existing audio checks for those inputs.

duration_ms.description: Native test-take cap in milliseconds (default 3000). It is always bounded; open-ended rehearsal is not supported.

fps.description: Capture rate for the disposable take (default 30).

monitor.description: Legacy display ordinal when no exact monitor_id is available.

monitor_id.description: Exact opaque monitor identity from the current screen_record.doctor row. It is revalidated and never falls back.

window.description: Exact opaque native window identity from the current screen_record.doctor row.

verbs.result: {playback_handle, playback_url, duration_ms, discard_on_start_recording:true, note} — playback_handle is an opaque, process-local capability for the one current temporary take and playback_url is its same-origin bounded route. Neither is a filesystem path; no media bytes, capture id, output directory, recovery item, project receipt, or promotion action is returned.

verbs.name: screen_record.rehearsal_discard
verbs.description: Idempotently revoke and delete the current disposable rehearsal take. With a handle, it must be the exact opaque playback_handle returned by rehearsal_start; without one, it safely discards whichever temporary rehearsal is current. A repeated cleanup for a recently discarded handle returns discarded:false rather than restoring or exposing bytes. It never accepts a path, project, media asset, capture id, or promotion instruction, and it never enters recovery inventory.

handle.description: Optional opaque playback_handle returned by screen_record.rehearsal_start. Omit for safe unmount cleanup of the current take.

verbs.result: {handle|null, discarded, state:"discarded"|"stopping"} — discarded:true revokes the opaque route immediately. state:stopping means a native take was signalled and still owns devices until its bounded worker exits; it never yields media or a path.
